title: threads.json — normalized provider review threads
description: One provider bundle's normalized PR-conversation feed, written beside the raw host files (inline.json/reviews.json keep their exact bytes). Each host's native review data is filtered the way its review surface expects (system/deleted/pending comments dropped, host resolution and stale-anchor state read from the host's own fields) and flattened to one shape, so re-review, address-reviews, merge readiness, and calibration read prior feedback without parsing six formats. Review threads are authoritative: GitHub comes from GraphQL reviewThreads (REST has no resolution), GitLab from discussions (resolved/resolvable), Azure from thread status, Forgejo from review-comment resolver/position, Bitbucket from comment resolution + inline.outdated, GitCafe from its comment flags. Unknown root keys are rejected: a new field is a contract change.

schema_version.description: Feed format version; only "1" is read.

provider.description: The host whose raw payload produced this feed.

pr.description: Pull request number the feed belongs to (0 when the positional was not numeric).

head_sha.description: The PR head the feed was read at; GitLab and Forgejo compare it to a comment's anchor commit to flag outdated.

fetched_at.description: UTC read timestamp (RFC 3339); the feed is a snapshot, not a live view.

truncated.description: True when a thread read failed, a host thread arrived with more comments than its cap returned, or a page walk stopped at the provider cap. The threads present are still trustworthy; the list may under-cover.

threads.description: One normalized thread per host root, in host order. A thread with a diff anchor is a review-comment; otherwise it is a conversation comment. Replies ride in comments[].

thread.description: One review thread or conversation comment: host thread identity (what a resolution call takes), diff anchor and state, root author, and the replies.

id.description: Host thread identity (GitHub reviewThreads id, GitLab discussion id, Bitbucket root comment id, Azure thread id, Forgejo comment id, GitCafe thread id). Empty when the payload carried none.

path.description: Diff-relative path for a review-comment, empty for a conversation comment.

line.description: End line of the anchor (the commented line for a single-line anchor), null when absent.

start_line.description: First line of a multi-line anchor, null for a single-line anchor or a host with no range field.

side.description: LEFT for a deleted-side anchor, RIGHT for an added/context anchor, null for a conversation comment or a host with no side.

resolved.description: Host resolution state read from the host's own field: GitHub isResolved, GitLab note resolved, Azure thread status, Forgejo review-comment resolver, Bitbucket comment resolution, GitCafe resolved/resolvedAt. Hosts without a resolution field read false.

outdated.description: True when the host says the anchor no longer maps to the current head: GitHub isOutdated, Bitbucket inline.outdated, GitLab position.head_sha differs from the feed head, Forgejo position 0 against a non-zero original_position, GitCafe outdated, Azure context without a line.

url.description: Host-comment permalink when the payload carries one cheaply (GitHub url, Forgejo html_url, Bitbucket links.html.href); null otherwise.

author.description: Root comment author handle or display name, empty when absent.

author_kind.description: verdict when the root comment's final line is verdict's own hidden marker, bot when the host marks the author as a bot (or the login carries GitHub's [bot] suffix), else human.

finding_sig.description: Finding signature linked from the root comment's hidden final-line verdict marker; null for threads verdict did not author and for summaries.

kind.description: review-comment for a diff-anchored thread, issue-comment for a conversation comment.

comments.description: Root comment first, then replies in host order. Each comment id is the id a reply call takes (GitHub databaseId).

comment.description: One comment inside a thread: author identity/kind, the body excerpt, and the truncation flag.

id.description: Host comment id (GitHub databaseId when present), empty when absent.

author.description: Author handle or display name, empty when absent.

author_kind.description: verdict when the comment's final line is verdict's own hidden marker, bot when the host marks the author as a bot (or the login carries GitHub's [bot] suffix), else human.

body.description: Comment body, capped at 8 KiB; the raw provider file keeps the full text.

truncated.description: True when body is an excerpt of a longer comment.

created_at.description: Host creation timestamp (RFC 3339 when the host publishes one), empty when absent.
